html:
Ahé is the name the map gives to a Kawahib group of northern Rondônia, in western Brazil, between the Madeira and Jaci-Paraná rivers. Little is recorded about a group of this name. Kawahib peoples speak languages of the Tupi-Guarani branch of the Tupian family.

Their relatives include the Jiahui, the Tenharim and the Envuga. Rubber tappers entered this part of the Madeira basin in the late 1800s, and later roads, dams and ranches cut into the forest.
